analysis.title: Early Morning Reid - Macro Strategy (11 November 2026)
key_insights: A strong US October CPI print and hawkish Fed comments drove a major Treasury selloff. The 2yr yield rose 17.6bps to 4.74%, its biggest daily jump since April 2025, and markets priced a modest chance of a 50bp Fed hike in December.

Core CPI rose +0.30% m/m in October versus +0.2% expected. It was the third straight month at +0.3%, and the 3-month annualised core pace is +3.75%, the fastest since April 2024. Headline CPI was +0.35% m/m versus +0.3% expected, with a 3-month annualised pace of +5.72%. There are no y/y figures because last year's October CPI was not published during the government shutdown.

Fed Governor Waller said before the release that if core CPI ran around 0.3% or higher, a 50bp hike should be considered in December, and that a 25bp hike would put Fed credibility at risk. Dallas Fed's Logan said the FOMC needs at least two more 25bp hikes. KC Fed's Schmid called the current policy rate fairly accommodative. Chicago Fed's Goolsbee called the print borderline disturbing.

Hikes priced for the December FOMC rose from 21.0bps on Monday to 27.7bps at the close and 28.5bps this morning. A 25bp hike is fully priced and futures show a 14% chance of 50bp. The September 2027 meeting rate rose 22.3bps on the day. DB economists added a January hike and now expect 25bp hikes in December, January and March.

The 10yr Treasury yield rose 10.8bps to 4.99%, its highest in nearly two weeks. The S&P 500 fell -0.38%, the Nasdaq -0.74% and the Mag-7 -0.83%. Nvidia fell -5.47%. The equal-weighted S&P 500 was only -0.02% and almost half of S&P constituents rose.

CoreWeave reported Q3 revenue of $3.66bn versus $3.56bn estimate and raised full-year revenue guidance to $13.0-13.3bn versus $12.9bn estimate. Shares rose over 7% after hours. S&P 500 futures were +0.65% and Nasdaq 100 futures +1.40% this morning.

Brent fell -1.17% to $91.49/bbl, its lowest since August, on hopes for a diplomatic resolution of the US-Iran conflict. The 12-month Brent future fell -1.68% to a two-month low of $77.64/bbl. Trump said the US is keeping things at the status quo at the request of Iran's neighbours.

The bond selloff spread globally. 10yr Bund +5.5bps, OAT +7.0bps, BTP +7.4bps, Japan 10yr +10.3bps to 2.78%, Australia +5.6bps, New Zealand +6.8bps. ECB December hike odds rose from 83% to 92%, and hikes priced by June 2027 rose 10.9bps to 58bps.

Asian equities rose overnight on the AI-trade optimism: KOSPI +2.27% and Nikkei +1.33%. The Hang Seng fell -0.83% and the CSI 300 and Shanghai Composite were flat. South Korea's October unemployment rate fell to 2.5% versus 2.6% expected.
US bond markets are closed today for Veterans Day. ECB speakers include Lagarde, Cipollone, Kazaks and Nagel. The only data release is Italian September industrial production.

market_movers.rationale: Nvidia fell -5.47% on the day and led the Nasdaq lower as yields rose.
CoreWeave beat Q3 revenue estimates ($3.66bn vs $3.56bn) and raised full-year guidance to $13.0-13.3bn versus $12.9bn estimate. Shares rose over 7% after hours.

earnings_insights: CoreWeave Q3 revenue reported $3.66bn versus $3.56bn consensus estimate. Full-year revenue guidance raised to $13.0-13.3bn versus $12.9bn consensus estimate. Shares +7% after hours, which eased some doubt around the AI cycle.
